content: This product may contain inactive ingredients that have the potential to cause allergic reactions or other complications. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used if it is clearly necessary. The oral form of this medication is known to pass into breast milk in small amounts, but it is not known whether the topical form of ivermectin passes into breast milk. Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. It is important to maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal supplements, and share this information with your doctor and pharmacist. If this medication is swallowed, it may be harmful. In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. To prevent the spread of lice, wash all recently used clothing, hats, bedding, and towels in hot water or have them dry-cleaned. Store this medication at room temperature and do not freeze it. This product is intended for single use only. Discard any unused lotion. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly dispose of this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. This medication is used to treat head lice, which are small insects that attach to the hair and feed on blood from the scalp. Head lice infestations can cause itching and irritation of the scalp. Ivermectin lotion is not recommended for use in children under six months of age. If you are using an over-the-counter product for self-treatment, carefully read and follow all instructions on the product packaging before use. If you have any questions, consult your pharmacist. Apply ivermectin lotion only to dry hair and scalp. Use enough lotion (up to one tube) to completely coat and cover all of your hair from the roots to the ends, as well as your entire scalp. Leave the lotion on for a full 10 minutes, then rinse it off with water. Children should have an adult apply this medication for them. Do not use this medication on your eyebrows or eyelashes. Avoid getting the medication in your eyes. If this occurs, flush your eyes with water. Do not swallow this medication. Do not use ivermectin lotion in your mouth, nose, vagina, or other areas of the body. This medication is for single use only. Discard any unused lotion. Possible side effects include eye redness or irritation, dry skin, or a stinging or burning sensation. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefit to you outweighs the risk of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before using ivermectin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. The oral form of this medication passes into breast milk in small amounts, but it is unknown if the topical form of ivermectin passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may change how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. If someone has overdosed and has serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911. Otherwise, call a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. To prevent the spread of lice, wash in hot water or dry clean all recently used clothing, hats, bedding, and towels. Store at room temperature. Do not freeze. This medication is for single use only. Throw away any unused lotion. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed.
